newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Trend number of NZ job ads remains weak - ANZ Bank.
newsitem.headline: Trend number of NZ job ads remains weak - ANZ Bank.

text.p: The trend number of New Zealand job ads rose 0.1 percent in November following a 0.5 percent fall in October, ANZ Bank said on Tuesday.
In annual terms, the trend number of job ads remained weak, with November's trend number 8.8 percent below November 1995.
ANZ said job advertisements had risen slightly in Auckland during November, but both Wellington and Christchurch continued to experience a decline in monthly job ad figures.
"The level of job advertisements in all the main centres is lower than a year ago, and ads in Wellington and Christchurch are below 1994 levels as well," ANZ said.
The monthly trend in job ads in Auckland rose 0.6 percent in November, following a 0.1 percent fall in October. In annual terms, the trend number of job ads was 6.9 percent lower than a year ago.
Job ads in Wellington fell 0.7 percent on the previous month, and 19.2 percent on a year ago.
Christchurch also recorded a decline in November, falling 1.4 percent, with the trend number of job ads 10.5 percent below November 1995.
The ANZ Job Ads Survey has been recording the number of job advertisements in a number of smaller regional newspapers since June 1994.
"Although there is not yet sufficient data to calculate a meaningful trend series, the job advertisement levels alone do provide some indication of employment conditions," the bank said.
Much of the strong job growth of the past couple of years had been concentrated in the main centres.
"Yet, while job advertisements in the non-metropolitan areas have not risen strongly over this period, neither do they currently appear to be declining sharply," ANZ said.
